majors.what: `applySlideInsert` stores the caller's `command.slide` object directly into the manifest (via `addSlide`), and `applyDeckSetTheme` (line 404) stores `command.theme` directly into `doc.theme`. Neither is copied. Verified empirically: after `history.apply([{t:'slide.insert', at:0, slide: entry, html:'h'}], origin)`, `history.doc.manifest.slides[entry.id] === entry` is `true`, and a subsequent `entry.title = 'HIJACKED'` changes the live document — no `rev` bump, no history entry, no patch. The same aliasing reaches the undo stack: `history.ts:234` does `const forward = [...commands]`, a shallow array copy that retains the caller's command objects, so mutating `cmd.html` after `apply` returns changes what `redo()` replays (verified: replays 'MUTATED').
majors.why: This falsifies the two load-bearing claims the layer is built on — commands.ts:2-4 ('nothing is allowed to reach into a deck and change it') and history.ts:13-16 ('a design that let a caller mutate the document beside the history would make every stacked inverse a guess'). It is not reachable today (no `DocumentSession` yet, and the eventual IPC path hands over fresh `JSON.parse` objects), which is why it is a major rather than a blocker — but the first main-process caller that builds a `SlideEntry`, applies it, and then keeps editing that object gets silent document corruption with a history stack that no longer describes reality. The copy discipline is already applied inconsistently in this same file, which marks it as an oversight rather than a decision: `deck.setMeta` copies `authors` (line 462) and `deck.setThemeTokens` copies `series` (line 436), and `deck.ts duplicateSlide` uses `structuredClone` for exactly this reason.
majors.fix: `structuredClone(command.slide)` before passing to `addSlide` in `applySlideInsert`, and `structuredClone(command.theme)` in `applyDeckSetTheme`. Optionally deep-copy in `history.ts:234` too, or state in the `apply` docblock that the caller surrenders ownership of the command objects.

majors.what: `open.inverse.unshift(...applied.inverse)` — the reverse-order accumulation that makes a multi-batch transaction undo correctly — is not pinned by any test. Mutation test: changing `unshift` to `push` leaves all 237 tests green while breaking the feature. With the mutant, a transaction of `[remove(s1)] , [move(s3,0)] , [move(s0,2)]` undoes to slide order `[s1,s0,s2,s3]` instead of the original `[s0,s1,s2,s3]`; the unmutated code restores exactly (verified both ways).
majors.why: 'A full agent turn is a single Ctrl+Z' (§5) is the reason transactions exist, and 'that Ctrl+Z restores the document exactly' is the only property that makes it safe. The existing test `collapses every batch in a turn into one undo step` (history.test.ts:227) uses batches whose inverses commute, so it pins the collapsing but not the ordering. Per the review standard, a change is untested if reverting the mechanism turns nothing red — this mechanism is one character away from a silent data-ordering regression, in the code path an AI turn always takes.
majors.fix: Add a transaction test whose batches do not commute — e.g. batch 1 removes a slide, batches 2-3 move others — and assert `toStrictEqual` against the pre-transaction document after `undo()`. The same test should assert the recorded `entry.inverse` command order (`move, move, insert`, not `insert, move, move`).

minors.what: Nit: the `entry.file !== slideFilePath(entry.id)` guard is unreachable. `SlideEntrySchema.superRefine` (types.ts:157-163) already rejects any entry whose `file` is not `slides/<id>.html`, and `SlideEntrySchema.safeParse` runs four lines earlier at line 269. Replacing the guard with `if (false)` leaves the suite green, and direct probing confirms the schema rejects both a mismatched-but-well-formed path and an arbitrary path.
minors.why: Dead code plus a comment that has drifted: lines 278-279 claim it 'catches the document-level half of the same invariant, where a caller hand-builds an entry from a stale id', but a stale id is precisely what the schema's superRefine already catches. A future reader will trust the comment and assume the schema is weaker than it is.
minors.fix: Delete the guard and its comment, or keep it and change the comment to say it is a defensive assertion the schema already covers.

minors.what: Nit: `mergeGroup` builds `{ ...current }` and `invertGroup` (line 511) builds `{}` — ordinary prototyped objects — while the file header (lines 41-45) states that 'every map this module builds is `Object.create(null)`'. Observable consequence: a `deck.setThemeTokens` patch naming a token `__proto__` returns `{ok: true}` having changed nothing (verified: token keys unchanged, `Object.hasOwn(tokens.color,'__proto__')` false), because assigning `next['__proto__'] = '#ffffff'` hits the prototype setter and is discarded.
minors.why: A command that 'succeeded' while changing nothing is the exact failure mode the docblock at lines 20-22 says this layer exists to prevent. Impact is small — token names come from an agent tool call and no model realistically emits `__proto__`, the inverse is symmetrically a no-op so history stays consistent, and I confirmed there is no actual pollution (an object-valued `__proto__` from `JSON.parse` is rejected by `parseTheme`, and global `Object.prototype` is untouched). It is the inaccurate invariant claim more than the behavior that costs time later.
minors.fix: Build both with `Object.create(null)`, or narrow the header claim to the slide-id-keyed maps it actually describes.

minors.what: Nit: the two deliberately-defensive branches are correct but untested — `undo()`'s early return on a failed `applyBatch` (line 267) and `abortTransaction()`'s leave-the-transaction-open path (line 347). Both mutants survive the suite: popping the entry before checking success, and closing the transaction anyway on rollback failure, each stay green.
minors.why: Both comments justify the branch by pointing at how unrecoverable the alternative is, so the branches carry real weight. I verified by hand that the real code behaves as documented (a refused undo leaves `rev`, the undo stack and the redo stack untouched), but nothing stops a later refactor from reordering the pop.
minors.fix: One test each, reaching the branch by corrupting an entry's `inverse` to an unapplicable command.

minors.what: Nit: the soft byte cap does not constrain an open transaction, and `commandBytes` (commands.ts:663) undercounts. With `maxBytes: 1000`, a 20-batch transaction retained 63,148 bytes during the turn and still 63,148 after commit, because the committed turn is a single entry and `#push`'s `length > 1` guard correctly refuses to evict it. Separately, a `slide.remove` entry is estimated at 301 bytes against 487 bytes of real serialized payload, since only `html`/`notes` string lengths are counted (in UTF-16 code units, not UTF-8 bytes) and the `SlideEntry` the inverse carries is folded into a 128-byte constant.
minors.why: Both are documented as deliberate ('a rough retained-bytes cost', 'a soft one'), so this is not a defect. Worth flagging only because the docblock justifies never-evict-the-newest as protecting 'the edit the user just made', and an entire agent turn — the largest thing this system produces — is also a single newest entry. The cap therefore bounds the stack but not the worst case it was written for.
minors.fix: None required. If it matters later, count the transaction's accumulated bytes against the cap while it is open, or note in the docblock that one turn is exempt by construction.

verification.typecheck: pnpm typecheck (tsc --noEmit for tsconfig.node.json and tsconfig.web.json) — exit 0
verification.test: pnpm test (vitest run) — exit 0, 10 files, 237 passed (matches the builder's claim)
verification.worktree: git status --porcelain clean before and after; all mutation tests restored from backup and re-verified green

hypotheses_tested: Round-trip totality — apply(invert(cmd,pre), apply(cmd,pre)) deep-equal pre for all 8 command types across empty deck, single slide, no-notes deck, themeless deck, themed deck with series, token-delete-via-null, series-null, meta-null, and explicit/implicit theme paths. REJECTED: every case exact under toStrictEqual. (An apparent failure on my first pass was my own fixture carrying a schema-invalid theme.)

Transaction undo is not exact — three non-commuting batches (remove, move, move) collapsed into one entry, then undone. REJECTED: deep-equal to the original. An initial `JSON.stringify` comparison said 'false', but that is key-insertion-order drift in `manifest.slides` after remove-then-reinsert, not a content difference; `toStrictEqual` passes. Worth knowing that a save after undo produces byte-different manifest JSON with identical content.

Transaction inverse ordering is unguarded — mutate `open.inverse.unshift` to `push` (history.ts:239). CONFIRMED as a coverage gap: suite stays green, undo of a 3-batch transaction produces the wrong slide order. Raised as major #2.

Caller-owned objects alias into the document and the undo stack. CONFIRMED: `doc.manifest.slides[entry.id] === entry` after `slide.insert`; post-hoc mutation of the caller's entry rewrites the live document, and post-hoc mutation of a command's `html` changes what redo replays. Raised as major #1.

Any code path mutates the input deck — every command and its inverse run against a recursively `Object.freeze`d document. REJECTED: no throws, no failures, all clean. Structural sharing is real (unchanged `manifest`, `notes`, `manifest.slides` shared by reference) and safe precisely because nothing writes in place.

Serializability — `JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(cmd))` applied against the same document for all 8 command types plus all 8 inverses. REJECTED: identical results in every case; commands are pure JSON data, so the §6 recovery journal can replay them.

Prototype-key discipline beyond setHtml — `__proto__`, `constructor` and `toString` as the slide id on `slide.setHtml`, `slide.remove`, `slide.move`, `slide.setNotes`, and as `slide.insert`'s entry id. REJECTED: every one returns `slide-not-found` (insert returns `invalid-slide-entry` via the id regex); none resolves a prototype member as data. A `constructor`-named *theme token* round-trips correctly; only `__proto__` as a token name is a silent no-op (minor #2).

Prototype pollution via a theme-token patch from a trust boundary — `JSON.parse('{"color":{"__proto__":{"pwned":"yes"}}}')`. REJECTED: `parseTheme` rejects the result, and global `Object.prototype` is never touched.

Precondition completeness — insert at length / length+1 / -1 / 1.5 / NaN, move to length / -1 / NaN, move on an empty deck, remove the last slide. REJECTED: append works, every out-of-range and non-integer index is `index-out-of-range`, move on an empty deck is `slide-not-found`, and removing the last slide yields `slideOrder: []` that round-trips exactly.

Generic preservation — a `DeckBundle`-shaped input with `extras` and `assets` through every command and through `applyBatch`. REJECTED: both survive by reference in all cases. An unknown forward-compat key on the manifest also survives `deck.setMeta`, confirming zod's stripped output is correctly discarded in favour of the constructed object.

Eviction can drop the newest entry, or land badly during a transaction. REJECTED on both counts: with `maxBytes: 10`, a single oversized entry survives and stays undoable; a second push evicts the older one FIFO; and `#push` is never called while a transaction is open, so no eviction can interleave with one.

Redo leaves stale byte accounting (history.ts:290 spreads `...entry`, keeping the old `bytes` while replacing `inverse`). REJECTED as unreachable: redo re-applies from exactly the state undo restored, so the recomputed inverse always equals the recorded one. The refresh is defensive but never observable.

Undo/redo/abort under interleaving — undo then new command then redo (`nothing-to-redo`, correct); a batch failing mid-transaction (aborts at the right index, document unchanged); abort after a partial turn (document restored exactly, no entry pushed, transaction closed); reset while open (transaction dropped). All REJECTED.
A failed undo corrupts the stacks — forced by corrupting an entry's inverse. REJECTED: `rev`, undo depth and redo depth all unchanged; the entry is not popped.

Exhaustiveness — added a 9th `DocCommand` variant. REJECTED as a risk: `noImplicitReturns` is on and `tsc` fails both `applyCommand` (line 478) and `invertCommand` (line 547) with TS2366. `commandBytes` has a `default` and is intentionally lenient.

Additional surviving mutants recorded as minors: the `entry.file` guard (commands.ts:280, equivalent mutant — schema already covers it), `abortTransaction`'s rollback-failure branch, and `undo`'s pop-after-check ordering. Mutants correctly caught: newest-never-evicted guard, `applyBatch` inverse ordering, `undo` transaction-open guard, notes-mismatch check, empty-transaction skip, and the duplicate-id check against `doc.slides`.
notes.plan_conformance: Conforms to 10-architecture.md §5 on the points that matter: commands are serializable data (verified by JSON round-trip, which §6's journal depends on), the inverse is a separate function computed against the pre-state, transactions collapse an agent turn into one undo step, an errored turn commits while abort is reserved for validation failures, and the caps are 200 entries / 64 MB cleared by reset. Three deviations, all documented in the file header with reasoning and all judged acceptable: `slide.patchHtml` and the 500 ms design-mode coalescing are deferred to 40-design-mode.md (no producer exists; the union is open and history treats entries opaquely, so it lands additively); `slide.setNotes` is widened to `string | null` and `deck.setThemeTokens` is added, both needed to make the inverse total; and invert lives in `src/shared/document/commands.ts` rather than §5's `src/main/document/invert.ts`, which is an improvement — 70-testing-ci.md requires pure logic to be reachable from Vitest, and shared placement matches M1.1's layout. Dependency direction is clean (`src/shared` imports only `./deck`, `./types`, `../slide-id`); no new dependencies; no `any`; the two `as` casts are commented and, in the `ThemeTokens` case, immediately validated by `parseTheme` rather than trusted.
notes.summary: Genuinely strong work — the inverse is total, atomicity holds, nothing mutates a frozen input, commands are pure JSON, prototype keys are rejected on every slide-id-keyed command, and every precondition I probed behaves correctly. Two things to fix before merge: the command layer stores caller-owned `SlideEntry` and `Theme` objects into the document by reference, which lets a future main-process caller edit the live deck behind the funnel's back; and the transaction inverse-ordering line — the one that makes an agent turn a correct single Ctrl+Z — survives mutation with the whole suite green.
